problem_text:
A manufacturing network aims to devise a production quality enhancement strategy to lower defect rates across several assembly lines. Initially, no corrective procedures have been implemented.

The attributes of each production line are as follows:
* For Line A, defect rate per unit is 2.065, output volume is 129.684.
* For Line B, defect rate per unit is 1.568, output volume is 154.081.
* For Line C, defect rate per unit is 1.739, output volume is 87.304.
* For Line D, defect rate per unit is 2.931, output volume is 144.115.
* For Line E, defect rate per unit is 2.854, output volume is 238.604.
* For Line F, defect rate per unit is 2.178, output volume is 168.38.
* For Line G, defect rate per unit is 2.465, output volume is 262.335.

To improve quality, several corrective procedures are available, each characterized by a specific defect reduction rate:
* Procedure Alpha reduces defects by 66%
* Procedure Beta reduces defects by 33%
* Procedure Gamma reduces defects by 26%
* Procedure Delta reduces defects by 17%
* Procedure Epsilon reduces defects by 45%
* Procedure Zeta reduces defects by 13%
* Procedure Eta reduces defects by 45%

Implementing a procedure on a line incurs an additional cost per unit of output. The cost matrix for all line–procedure combinations is detailed below:

| Line \ Procedure | Alpha | Beta | Gamma | Delta | Epsilon | Zeta | Eta |
|--|-|-|-|-|-|-|
| Line A | 35.478 | 56.143 | 48.634 | 132.874 | 185.223 | 170.955 | 27.568 |
| Line B | 147.671 | 46.192 | 61.008 | 137.998 | 124.555 | 175.988 | 45.751 |
| Line C | 154.722 | 147.618 | 116.182 | 101.085 | 175.2 | 73.263 | 191.834 |
| Line D | 12.913 | 188.06 | 192.795 | 32.29 | 199.919 | 100.995 | 56.093 |
| Line E | 124.836 | 48.857 | 183.874 | 114.895 | 157.348 | 82.326 | 111.394 |
| Line F | 78.259 | 59.697 | 107.435 | 104.483 | 28.736 | 196.451 | 99.203 |
| Line G | 169.549 | 183.723 | 80.434 | 88.647 | 116.88 | 52.042 | 37.725 |

Management must decide how to assign corrective procedures to each line (lines may adopt multiple procedures concurrently), and it is permissible for a line to remain partially uncorrected if required. The objective is to guarantee that the total defect count is lowered by at least a proportion P = 0.33 of the initial defect level, while minimizing the aggregate implementation cost.
